Incident Bot: PAGE: PagerDuty alert fired -> scale_controller_throttle (service=inference-gateway) severity=P1 link: https://pagerduty.example/alerts/PD-78901
PagerDuty: Alert routed to #eng-oncall via policy=infra-inference-escalation
Maya S.: acked on PD, I'm on it. First check: queue depth and pending pods
Jordan R.: I see ~8.6k queued messages on inference-queue in us-west-2, pod Pending count ~95 (`kubectl get pods -n inference | grep Pending | wc -l`)
Lena Ops: scale-controller logs show repeated failures creating nodes: `createInstance: 429 rateLimitExceeded` across three provider accounts
Tom D.: noticed dropped websocket connects and a spike in 5xx from frontend LB, likely from queue timeout
Maya S.: running step 1 of runbook: toggle emergency-shedder to reject best-effort requests and lower concurrency for medium-tier customers -> flipping feature flag now
Deploy Bot: emergency flag toggle submitted: flag-id ff-331, rolling out to inference-gateway (canary -> all)
Jordan R.: enabling manual growth on nodepool: `gcloud container node-pools resize inference-dedicated --num-nodes=50` but controller also trying to create nodes, might exacerbate rate limits
Maya S.: hold on manual resize, Eng-Platform please confirm if we should pause automated autoscale attempts first
Eng-Platform: responding - pause autoscaler? We recommend pausing the controller's concurrent-create worker and use staggered manual increments to respect provider rate limits; initiating hotfix to add exponential backoff to create calls
Tom D.: rolling traffic rules: divert non-critical traffic to fallback-model (lower cost but CPU-only) to reduce new request load; update applied
CS Team: opened customer incident notifications for impacted customers (IDs: C-443, C-452) with note: degraded streaming for some requests, working on mitigation
Maya S.: after shedding, queue dropped to ~4.1k, but pod pending still ~60; kube events show `FailedCreatePod -> failed to find capacity` and `FailedCreatePod -> quota exceeded` depending on provider account
Jordan R.: grabbing logs from scale-controller:
```
E2026 scale-controller.go: failed to create node: 429 RateLimitExceeded
retry_count=6 last_error=quotaExceeded
RequestIDs=[r1 r2 r3]
```
Eng-Platform: we requested emergency quota bump from provider; meanwhile we can commission preemptible instances in an alternate project/account we control to bypass per-account throttling. Will coordinate IAM and CNI tweaks
Maya S.: doing manual channeling: enabling alternate-nodepool in project-alt (preemptible) and scheduling a shallow drain for non-critical pods to free capacity
Deploy Bot: nodepool creation job submitted (job id create-pp-412)
Lena Ops: nodes from the alternate pool are registering, but kube-proxy metrics show flapping for a minute; scheduling delays observed
Jordan R.: manually evicting stuck pods to force scheduling onto new nodes (`kubectl delete pod ...`) — some services came up, queue now 1.2k
Tom D.: confirming upstream LB 5xx rate dropped to near-normal after routing changes
Maya S.: patching scale-controller in canary with improved create retry backoff and jitter; if stable we'll promote to prod to avoid reoccurrence
Eng-Platform: hotfix applied to canary; metrics show successful node creates without hitting 429s on canary account
CS Team: updated customer notices with ETA ~25m for full recovery; customers asked to open support if they see ongoing errors
Maya S.: starting to step down manual overrides; keeping alternate pool for 1 hour as buffer. Creating follow-up tasks: link to incident ticket INT-2026-331
Jordan R.: timeline note for postmortem: correlate with last-night's load-test burst that increased concurrent node create attempts during autoscaler warm-up
Lena Ops: suggest new alerts: provider-429-rate and consecutive-create-failures to trigger earlier escalation to Eng-Platform
Tom D.: recommended product change: emergency capacity button in Console that creates pre-warmed nodes in alternate account
Maya S.: closing PD incident in 10m if no regressions; leaving 30m watch. Assigning owners for postmortem: Maya S., Eng-Platform, Jordan R.
